witchetty-grub.name: Witchetty grub
witchetty-grub.summary: Large, white, wood-eating moth larvae eaten in Australia, historically a staple food in the diets of Aboriginal Australians.

quandong.name: Quandong
quandong.summary: Common name mainly for Santalum acuminatum, a desert tree species valued especially for its edible fruit.

backhousia-citriodora.name: Lemon myrtle
backhousia-citriodora.summary: A flowering plant native to subtropical Queensland, Australia, valued as a lemon-scented spice.

tetragonia-tetragonioides.name: Warrigal greens
tetragonia-tetragonioides.summary: A leafy flowering plant native to eastern Asia, Australia and New Zealand, often cultivated as a vegetable; it grows well on sandy, salty coastal ground.

first-fleet.name: First Fleet
first-fleet.summary: Eleven British ships that carried over 1,400 convicts, marines and settlers to Australia in 1787–1788, founding the first British colony at Port Jackson.

botany-bay.name: Botany Bay
botany-bay.summary: An oceanic bay near Sydney, Australia, where James Cook first landed in 1770 and which the British later chose as the site of a penal colony.

james-cook.name: James Cook
james-cook.summary: A British Royal Navy officer, explorer and cartographer (1728-1779) who led three Pacific voyages, completed the first European circumnavigation of New Zealand's main islands, and led the first European visits to eastern Australia and Hawaii.

hms-endeavour.name: HMS Endeavour
hms-endeavour.summary: The Royal Navy research ship James Cook commanded to Tahiti, New Zealand and Australia from 1768 to 1771, becoming the first European vessel to reach Australia's east coast.

poverty-bay.name: Poverty Bay
poverty-bay.summary: The largest of several small bays on New Zealand's North Island, home to the Māori tribes Te Aitanga-a-Māhaki, Rongowhakaata and Ngāi Tāmanuhiri, with the city of Gisborne on its northern shore.

makassan-contact-with-australia.name: Makassan trepangers
makassan-contact-with-australia.summary: Makassarese and Sama-Bajau traders from Southern Sulawesi who began visiting northern Australia around the mid-18th century to collect and process trepang, or sea cucumber, for Chinese markets.

aotearoa.name: Aotearoa
aotearoa.summary: The Māori-language name for New Zealand, often translated as 'land of the long white cloud,' now widely used in bilingual naming of institutions.

bay-of-plenty.name: Bay of Plenty
bay-of-plenty.summary: A large bay on New Zealand's North Island, named by James Cook in 1769 after seeing the abundant food at nearby Māori villages.

sydney-parkinson.name: Sydney Parkinson
sydney-parkinson.summary: A Scottish botanical illustrator, about 1745 to 1771, who was the first European artist to visit Australia, New Zealand and Tahiti.

joseph-banks.name: Joseph Banks
joseph-banks.summary: English naturalist who sailed with Captain Cook, later serving as president of the Royal Society for over 41 years and turning Kew into the world's leading botanical garden.

george-stubbs.name: George Stubbs
george-stubbs.summary: Self-trained English painter (1724–1806) best known for his depictions of horses and other animals, informed by his study of anatomy.

the-kongouro-from-new-holland.name: The Kongouro from New Holland
the-kongouro-from-new-holland.summary: A George Stubbs oil painting of a kangaroo, the first depiction of an Australian animal in Western art, commissioned by Joseph Banks after Cook's first voyage.

arnhem-land.name: Arnhem Land
arnhem-land.summary: A remote region of Australia's Northern Territory, named after a Dutch ship in 1623 and home mostly to Aboriginal Australians, many living in small communities with little Western influence.

hawkesbury-river.name: Hawkesbury River
hawkesbury-river.summary: A river northwest of Sydney, Australia, traditionally used by Aboriginal peoples such as the Darug for food and trade, and the site of colonial farms from 1795.

dharug.name: Darug people
dharug.summary: An Aboriginal Australian people who lived as hunters around present-day Sydney before European settlement, later clashing violently with English settlers in the early 19th century.

marc-joseph-marion-du-fresne.name: Marion du Fresne
marc-joseph-marion-du-fresne.summary: French explorer (1724-1772) whose expedition made discoveries in Tasmania and New Zealand while seeking Terra Australis, and who was killed during his stay in New Zealand.

arthur-phillip.name: Arthur Phillip
arthur-phillip.summary: A Royal Navy officer (1738–1814) who became the first governor of the Colony of New South Wales, leading the First Fleet to found a settlement at Port Jackson.

pemulwuy.name: Pemulwuy
pemulwuy.summary: A Bidjigal warrior of the Dharug Nation (c. 1750–1802) and one of the most famous Aboriginal resistance fighters, who waged a twelve-year guerrilla war against British colonists.

parramatta.name: Parramatta
parramatta.summary: A city west of Sydney founded as a British settlement in 1788, the oldest inland European settlement in Australia.

watkin-tench.name: Watkin Tench
watkin-tench.summary: A British officer (1758–1833) who published two accounts of the First Fleet's voyage and the early colony at Port Jackson, providing a valued record of Australia's founding years.

robert-hughes-critic.name: Robert Hughes
robert-hughes-critic.summary: Australian art critic and documentary maker (1938-2012), once called 'the most famous art critic in the world', known for The Shock of the New on modern art and The Fatal Shore on Australia's convict history.

thomas-keneally.name: Thomas Keneally
thomas-keneally.summary: Australian novelist born 1935, best known for Schindler's Ark, about Oskar Schindler's rescue of Jews, later filmed as Schindler's List.

bennelong.name: Bennelong
bennelong.summary: A senior Eora man (c. 1764–1813) who served as an interlocutor between Aboriginal Australians and British colonists, becoming the first Aboriginal Australian to visit Europe and return.

abel-tasman.name: Abel Tasman
abel-tasman.summary: Dutch seafarer employed by the Dutch East India Company who in 1642 became the first European to reach New Zealand and Tasmania, naming the latter Van Diemen's Land after his patron.

robert-southey.name: Robert Southey
robert-southey.summary: English Romantic poet (1774–1843) and Poet Laureate from 1813 until his death, remembered for "After Blenheim" and the original "Goldilocks and the Three Bears".

jonathan-swift.name: Jonathan Swift
jonathan-swift.summary: Irish satirist, essayist and Anglican cleric (1667–1745) best known for Gulliver's Travels, regarded as one of the greatest satirists in English literature.

houyhnhnm.name: Houyhnhnm
houyhnhnm.summary: A fictional race of intelligent horses from the final part of Jonathan Swift's 1726 satirical novel Gulliver's Travels.

wiradjuri.name: Wiradjuri
wiradjuri.summary: Group of Aboriginal Australian people from central New South Wales, united by shared descent and traditions, historically skilled hunter-fisher-gatherers.

anita-heiss.name: Anita Heiss
anita-heiss.summary: An Aboriginal Australian author, poet and cultural activist born in 1968, known for advocating Indigenous Australian literature and literacy.

transit-of-venus.name: Transit of Venus
transit-of-venus.summary: A rare astronomical event in which Venus passes across the face of the Sun, historically used to calculate the distance from Earth to Venus and the scale of the solar system.

pleiades.name: Pleiades
pleiades.summary: An open star cluster in the constellation Taurus, about 444 light-years away, the brightest star cluster visible to the naked eye and known since antiquity as the Seven Sisters.

new-south-wales.name: New South Wales
new-south-wales.summary: A state on Australia's east coast whose capital, Sydney, is the country's most populous city; it began in 1788 as a British penal colony covering most of the mainland.

sir-john-pringle-1st-baronet.name: Sir John Pringle
sir-john-pringle-1st-baronet.summary: A Scottish physician (1707–1782) sometimes described as the 'father of military medicine.'

pitjantjatjara.name: Pitjantjatjara
pitjantjatjara.summary: An Aboriginal Australian people originating from the Central Australian desert near Uluru, closely related to the Yankunytjatjara and Ngaanyatjarra.

james-lind.name: James Lind
james-lind.summary: Scottish naval physician (1716-1794) who ran one of the first clinical trials, developing the theory that citrus fruit cured scurvy, and later led one of the world's largest naval hospitals.

duyfken.name: Duyfken
duyfken.summary: Small Dutch ship whose 1606 voyage under Willem Janszoon made the first authenticated European landing on the Australian mainland.

willem-janszoon.name: Willem Janszoon
willem-janszoon.summary: Dutch navigator (c. 1570–c. 1630) who in 1605–1606 became the first European known to see and land on the coast of Australia.

lu-s-vaz-de-torres.name: Luís Vaz de Torres
lu-s-vaz-de-torres.summary: A Spanish expedition captain, born around 1565, who made the first recorded European navigation of the strait between Australia and New Guinea, now named Torres Strait after him.

torres-strait.name: Torres Strait
torres-strait.summary: Strait between Australia and New Guinea, named after Spanish navigator Luís Vaz de Torres, who sailed through it in 1606.

terra-nullius.name: Terra nullius
terra-nullius.summary: A Latin legal principle meaning 'nobody's land,' used since the 19th century to justify claiming territory not held by a recognized sovereign state, including land where indigenous peoples lived.

van-diemen-s-land.name: Van Diemen's Land
van-diemen-s-land.summary: Colonial name for Tasmania during 19th-century European settlement, first reached by Abel Tasman in 1642, known for harsh penal colonies before being renamed in 1856.

george-iii.name: George III
george-iii.summary: King of Great Britain and Ireland from 1760 to 1820, whose reign saw victory over France in the Seven Years' War but the loss of Britain's American colonies.

the-dreaming.name: The Dreaming
the-dreaming.summary: Term coined by early anthropologists for the religio-cultural worldview of Australian Aboriginal mythology, an "Everywhen" when ancestral figures created the land; also used for personal totemic Dreamings such as the Honey Ant Dreaming.

makassar.name: Makassar
makassar.summary: Port city on the island of Sulawesi in Indonesia, historically the seat of the Gowa Sultanate and a major trading hub before Dutch conquest in the 17th century.

mircea-eliade.name: Mircea Eliade
mircea-eliade.summary: Romanian historian of religion, novelist and philosopher (1907–1986) who taught at the University of Chicago and developed influential theories on sacred myth and ritual.

torres-strait-islanders.name: Torres Strait Islanders
torres-strait-islanders.summary: Indigenous Melanesian peoples of the Torres Strait Islands, ethnically distinct from Aboriginal Australians, known for a seafaring culture and strong traditions in sculpture and mask-making.

songline.name: Songline
songline.summary: A path across the land, recorded in song, story, dance and art, that Aboriginal Australian belief holds was followed by ancestral creator-beings.

kimberley-western-australia.name: The Kimberley
kimberley-western-australia.summary: The northernmost of Western Australia's nine regions, bordered by the Indian Ocean and the Timor Sea, named in 1879 after the Earl of Kimberley.

yol-u.name: Yolŋu
yol-u.summary: Aboriginal Australian people of north-eastern Arnhem Land in the Northern Territory, whose clans belong to either the Dhuwa or Yirritja moiety.

endeavour-river.name: Endeavour River
endeavour-river.summary: River system on Cape York Peninsula in Far North Queensland, Australia, where James Cook's ship Endeavour was beached for repairs in 1770.

possession-island-queensland.name: Possession Island
possession-island-queensland.summary: A small island in Australia's Torres Strait where, in 1770, James Cook held a ceremony claiming Australia's east coast for Britain.

makassarese-language.name: Makassarese language
makassarese-language.summary: Austronesian language of the Makassarese people of South Sulawesi, Indonesia, with about 2.1 million native speakers as of 2000.

tobias-furneaux.name: Tobias Furneaux
tobias-furneaux.summary: British Royal Navy officer and navigator (1735-1781) who accompanied James Cook on his second voyage and was one of the first to circumnavigate the world in both directions.

hms-resolution-1771.name: HMS Resolution
hms-resolution-1771.summary: A Royal Navy sloop converted from a merchant collier, used by Captain James Cook for his second and third voyages of exploration in the Pacific, who called it his ship of choice.

bruny-island.name: Bruny Island
bruny-island.summary: Coastal island of Tasmania, Australia, near Hobart, named after the French explorer Antoine Bruni d'Entrecasteaux.

aboriginal-tasmanians.name: Aboriginal Tasmanians
aboriginal-tasmanians.summary: Indigenous people of Tasmania, isolated from mainland Aboriginal groups for about 8,000 years after rising seas flooded the Bass Strait around 6000 BCE; devastated after British colonisation began in 1803.

cooktown-queensland.name: Cooktown
cooktown-queensland.summary: Coastal town in Queensland, Australia, at the mouth of the Endeavour River, where James Cook beached his ship for repairs in 1770; founded as a town in 1873.

bungaree.name: Bungaree
bungaree.summary: Indigenous Australian Awabakal man (c. 1775–1830), explorer, entertainer, and community leader; the first person recorded as Australian and the first Australian-born person to circumnavigate the Australian mainland.

matthew-flinders.name: Matthew Flinders
matthew-flinders.summary: British navigator (1774–1814) who led the first inshore circumnavigation of Australia and is credited with popularising the continent's name.
